findings.reason: each move removes a real duplicate owner, the plan justifies the core layer owning identity so the crew layer cannot fork it, and the width is the price of one definition of identity, which the section argues for; a boundary would be a refinement, not a correction.
findings.text: §17 lands the span parser's generalisation, the `plan_headings` reader, a public machinery-element predicate, the identity derivation, the spelling grammar, the number core, the landed-card recogniser and thirteen moved tag helpers into `reckon/_plan_html.py`, a module that already carries `read_state`/`write_state`/`to_html` and the whole state model; the plan names no boundary between document-structure parsing and state modelling, so the module grows in two directions at once — a reviewer cannot see the one deep interface the section claims because it is now one of several over the same file

findings.reason: the interface_budget item exists so a reviewer can verify the added surface from the section's own text against the supplied figures, and here the arithmetic that carries that check does not reconcile, so an author must restate the count before a reviewer can confirm §16 and §17 account for their +3.
findings.text: §16's interface accounting reads "the family grows by four from the base before §18 landed, so three remain over the 1478 §18 left" and then enumerates four additions (the tag-stripper in §16, the heading reader and the machinery-element predicate in §17, and the classification predicate in §18), but §18's classification predicate is already inside the 1478, so the "three remain" count and the four-name list contradict each other and neither the "four" nor the "three" can be reproduced from the section's text

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the parser does hide one private raw-text read behind `plan_headings` (deep), but the design also keeps `structured_section_spans` public, adds a second public predicate, and moves thirteen helpers into a module that already owns the entire plan state model, widening the surface rather than deepening one boundary.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — each consolidation names the owner to extend and its file: `_TAG_RE` in reckon/_plan_html.py, `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` moving out of reckon/crew/routing.py, `landed_section_ids` moving out of reckon/_store.py, `doccheck._LANDED_SECTION_CLASS` folding onto the one class constant, and the three inline store grammars folding onto `is_section_identity` in reckon/_schema.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds `strip_tags` and §17 adds `plan_headings` and the machinery predicate (net +3 over the post-§18 base), and although §16 states why nothing is retired, its own counts do not reconcile so the section cannot be checked from its text alone.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism §16 and §17 say they extend exists as cited; I opened `_TAG_RE` and `count_open_decisions` (reckon/_plan_html.py:1506,1514), `_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`/`_AuthoredProseParser` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:147,168), `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`/`section_anchor` (reckon/crew/routing.py:224,238,243), `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` (reckon/_plan_html.py:44,94), the nine store helpers §17 moves (reckon/_store.py:848–1093), `landed_section_ids` (reckon/_store.py:1075) and `is_section_identity` (reckon/_schema.py:372), all present.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §16 names why the existing `_TAG_RE` expression and `count_open_decisions` cannot be extended instead of adding `strip_tags` (a decision rationale that is empty but for an entity reads non-empty today, so the richer stripper would flip the open-decision count), which is the justification the item requires.
